title: Creamy Tomato & Basil Pasta
description: A silky, rich tomato sauce with fresh basil — weeknight comfort in 25 minutes.
steps: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Cook the spaghetti according to packet instructions.
Dice the onion and finely chop the garlic. Heat olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the chopped tomatoes, season well, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the double cream and most of the basil. Simmer for 2 more minutes.
Reserve a cup of pasta water, then drain. Add the pasta to the sauce with a splash of pasta water and toss to coat.
Serve topped with parmesan and the remaining fresh basil.
tips: The pasta water is key — the starch helps the sauce cling beautifully.
Use a full-fat double cream for the richest result.
For a vegan version, swap cream for oat cream and skip the parmesan.
storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 3 days.
reheating: Reheat in a pan with a splash of water to loosen the sauce.

title: Spinach & Ricotta Pasta
description: Creamy ricotta and wilted spinach tossed with pasta and a hint of lemon — ready in 20 minutes.
steps: Cook the penne in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the crushed garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the spinach and wilt for 2 minutes, stirring. Season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg.
Remove from heat and stir in the ricotta, lemon zest, and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Add the drained pasta and enough pasta water to make a creamy, loose sauce.
Serve immediately with plenty of parmesan grated on top.
tips: Room-temperature ricotta blends more smoothly than cold.
Don't let the garlic brown — a pale gold is perfect.
Add chilli flakes for a bit of heat.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Leftovers keep for 2 days in the fridge.
reheating: Gently reheat in a pan with a splash of milk or water.

title: Creamy Mushroom & Garlic Pasta
description: Earthy chestnut mushrooms in a garlicky cream sauce with fresh thyme — pure comfort.
steps: Cook the tagliatelle in salted boiling water. Reserve pasta water before draining.
Melt the butter in a wide pan over high heat. Add the mushrooms in a single layer — don't stir for 2 minutes to let them brown.
Stir the mushrooms, add the sliced garlic and thyme leaves. Cook for 2 more minutes.
Pour in the cream and bring to a simmer. Cook for 3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Add the drained pasta to the pan with a splash of pasta water. Toss well.
Serve with lots of parmesan and freshly cracked black pepper.
tips: Don't crowd the mushrooms — browning them properly is what makes this dish.
A splash of dry white wine or vermouth before the cream is a lovely addition.
Dried porcini mushrooms soaked in hot water and added with the cream make this even more intense.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.
reheating: Reheat gently in a pan with a little extra cream or water.

title: Quick Puttanesca
description: Punchy, briny, and deeply satisfying. Olives, capers, and tomatoes — no fuss, all flavour.
steps: Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente.
Warm the olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the sliced garlic and chilli flakes; sizzle for 1 minute.
Add the capers and olives, stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the tomatoes, season, and simmer for 12 minutes until reduced and rich.
Drain the pasta, reserving some water, and toss into the sauce. Add a splash of pasta water to loosen.
Serve immediately — this dish needs no cheese.
tips: Rinse capers if they're packed in salt, not brine.
The sauce improves dramatically with a good simmer — don't rush it.
Left over sauce is brilliant on toast the next morning.
storage: Sauce keeps in the fridge for 4 days.
reheating: Reheat sauce in a pan, cook fresh pasta.

title: Lemon Courgette Orzo
description: Orzo simmered in vegetable stock with courgette, feta, and bright lemon — light and summery.
equipment: Wide saucepan or deep frying pan
steps: Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Grate in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Grate the courgettes and add to the pan. Cook for 3 minutes until softened.
Add the orzo and stir to coat in the oil. Pour in the stock, bring to a boil then simmer for 10-12 minutes, stirring often, until orzo is tender and stock is absorbed.
Squeeze in the lemon juice and add the zest. Season well.
Crumble over the feta and scatter with torn mint leaves.
Serve straight from the pan.
tips: Stir frequently — orzo sticks if left unattended.
Add more stock if it thickens too quickly.
A handful of frozen peas stirred in at the end adds colour and protein.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days — add a splash of stock when reheating.
reheating: Reheat in a pan with a little water or stock.

title: Easy Chickpea & Tomato Curry
description: A rich, spiced curry with protein-packed chickpeas — on the table in 25 minutes.
steps: Cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Dice the onion and finely chop the garlic and ginger. Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft. Add garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute.
Add the curry powder and garam masala. Stir for 30 seconds to toast the spices.
Pour in the tomatoes and coconut milk. Drain and rinse the chickpeas and add them.
Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens.
Season well and serve over rice, scattered with fresh coriander.
tips: For extra depth, stir in a tablespoon of mango chutney at the end.
Leftovers taste even better the next day.
Serve with a dollop of yoghurt and flatbread for a more complete meal.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. Freezes well.
reheating: Reheat in a pan with a splash of water for 5 minutes.

title: Saag Paneer
description: Golden pan-fried paneer nestled in a vibrant, spiced spinach sauce.
steps: Cook the basmati rice. Cut the paneer into 2cm cubes.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan over high heat. Fry the paneer until golden on both sides, around 2-3 minutes per side. Set aside.
In the same pan with 1 tbsp oil, sizzle the cumin seeds for 30 seconds. Add the diced onion and cook for 5 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute. Add garam masala and ground coriander.
Wilt the spinach in batches, then use a stick blender to partially blend (keeping some texture).
Stir in the cream and return the paneer to the pan. Simmer for 3 minutes.
Season and serve over basmati rice.
tips: Pressing the paneer with a cloth before frying helps it brown better.
Don't fully blend the spinach — some texture is important.
Add a fresh green chilli with the garlic for more heat.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.
reheating: Reheat gently in a pan, adding a splash of water if needed.

title: Sweet Potato & Red Lentil Dahl
description: A warming, nourishing dahl with sweet potato and coconut — deeply satisfying and vegan.
steps: Peel and dice the sweet potato into 2cm cubes. Dice the onion, mince the garlic and ginger.
Heat oil in a large pan. Add cumin seeds and sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, turmeric, and garam masala. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potato, lentils, tomatoes, coconut milk, and stock. Stir well.
Bring to a boil then simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until lentils are soft and sweet potato is tender.
Stir in the spinach to wilt. Season and serve with rice or naan.
tips: Rinse the lentils well before adding.
This freezes brilliantly — make double and freeze half.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon for brightness.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. Freezes for 3 months.
reheating: Reheat in a pan with extra stock or water.

title: Butter-Style Paneer Curry
description: Velvety, mildly spiced tomato-butter sauce with golden paneer. A crowd-pleasing favourite.
steps: Cook the rice. Cut the paneer into 2cm cubes and fry in butter until golden on all sides. Set aside.
In the same pan, cook the diced onion for 5 minutes. Add garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato purée and garam masala. Stir for 1 minute.
Add the canned tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes. Use a stick blender to blend smooth.
Stir in the cream and bring to a gentle simmer. Return the paneer to the pan.
Cook for 5 minutes. Season and serve over rice.
tips: Blending the sauce smooth is what makes this feel restaurant-quality.
A pinch of sugar balances the tomatoes.
Serve with naan bread to mop up the sauce.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.
reheating: Reheat gently in a pan over low heat.

title: Thai Green Tofu Curry
description: Fragrant coconut curry with crispy tofu and fresh veg — vibrant and ready in 25 minutes.
steps: Cook the rice. Press the tofu dry with kitchen paper and cut into cubes.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat. Fry the tofu until golden on all sides, around 5 minutes. Set aside.
In the same wok, fry the curry paste for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and bring to a simmer. Add the sliced courgette and pepper.
Simmer for 5 minutes. Add the tofu back in. Season with soy sauce and lime juice.
Serve over jasmine rice, with extra lime wedges.
tips: Pressing tofu is essential for crispiness — use a clean tea towel and weight it for 10 minutes.
Buy good-quality Thai green curry paste (Mae Ploy is widely available).
Add a handful of baby spinach or frozen peas for extra veg.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
reheating: Reheat in a pan over medium heat.

title: Mixed Veg Korma
description: A mild, creamy korma loaded with cauliflower and potato — perfect for the whole family.
steps: Cook the rice. Dice the potato into 2cm chunks and cut the cauliflower into florets.
Heat oil in a large pan. Cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the korma paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the potato, cauliflower, coconut milk, and ground almonds. Stir well.
Simmer for 20 minutes until potato is tender. Add the peas for the final 3 minutes.
Serve over rice, scattered with fresh coriander.
tips: A shop-bought korma paste is absolutely fine — Patak's is excellent.
Add a squeeze of lemon at the end for brightness.
Swap potato for sweet potato for a slightly different flavour.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days.
reheating: Reheat in a pan with a splash of water.

title: Crispy Onion Tarka Dhal
description: Comforting red lentil dhal finished with a sizzling tarka of crispy onions and cumin.
steps: Rinse the lentils. Simmer with stock, turmeric, half the garlic and ginger for 20 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomatoes and season well. Keep warm.
For the tarka: heat 3 tbsp oil in a small pan until very hot. Fry 1 sliced onion until deeply golden and crispy, around 8 minutes.
Add the remaining garlic, ginger, and cumin seeds. Sizzle for 1 minute.
Pour the tarka over the dhal. Stir half of it through and leave the rest on top.
Serve with warm naan and plenty of fresh coriander.
tips: The tarka (tempering) is what elevates this from ordinary to extraordinary.
Let the onion get properly golden — it should look almost burnt at the edges.
Dhal thickens as it cools — stir in more stock when reheating.
storage: Keeps for 4 days refrigerated. Freezes well.
reheating: Reheat in a pan with extra stock.

title: Pad Thai-Style Noodles
description: Stir-fried rice noodles with egg, beansprouts, crunchy peanuts, and zingy lime.
steps: Soak the rice noodles in boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Heat the wok over very high heat. Add oil and the garlic, stir for 30 seconds.
Push to the side and scramble the eggs in the centre. Let them set slightly before breaking up.
Add the noodles and toss to combine. Pour in the soy sauce and sriracha.
Toss for 2 minutes, adding a splash of water if needed.
Add beansprouts and half the spring onions. Toss for 1 more minute.
Serve topped with crushed peanuts, remaining spring onions, coriander, and lime wedges.
tips: A very hot wok is essential — the noodles should sizzle, not steam.
Have all ingredients prepped before you turn on the heat.
Fish sauce (1 tbsp) adds authentic depth if you have it.
storage: Best eaten immediately.
reheating: Not ideal for reheating, but a quick toss in a hot wok works.

title: Teriyaki Mushroom Noodles
description: Glossy teriyaki sauce coating egg noodles, meaty mushrooms, and tender-crisp broccoli.
steps: Cook the noodles according to packet instructions, rinse with cold water and drain.
Mix the soy sauce and mirin together to make the teriyaki sauce.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok over high heat. Fry the sliced mushrooms for 4 minutes without stirring until browned.
Add the broccoli florets with 2 tbsp water. Stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger, stir for 1 minute. Add the noodles and teriyaki sauce.
Toss everything together for 2 minutes. Drizzle with sesame oil.
Serve topped with spring onions and sesame seeds.
tips: Mirin can be replaced with 1 tbsp honey + 1 tbsp soy sauce in a pinch.
Don't stir the mushrooms immediately — let them brown for maximum flavour.
Add chilli flakes for a spicy version.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days.
reheating: Toss in a hot wok with a splash of water.

title: Easy Miso Ramen
description: Deeply savoury miso broth with silky tofu, soft-boiled eggs, and springy noodles.
steps: Soft-boil the eggs: simmer in water for exactly 6 minutes, then transfer to cold water. Peel when cool.
Bring the stock to a simmer. Whisk in the miso paste (don't boil after adding miso).
Add soy sauce and sesame oil. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Cook the ramen noodles in a separate pan of boiling water. Drain.
Cut the tofu into cubes. Slice the spring onions.
Divide noodles between bowls. Ladle over the hot miso broth.
Top with tofu, halved soft-boiled eggs, sweetcorn, and spring onions.
tips: Never boil the broth after adding miso — it kills the beneficial probiotics.
Marinate the tofu briefly in soy sauce for extra flavour.
Add a sheet of nori and a drizzle of chilli oil to finish.
storage: Store broth and noodles separately for up to 2 days.
reheating: Gently reheat broth, cook fresh noodles.

title: Sesame Greens & Soba Noodles
description: Cold soba noodles with edamame, broccoli, and a punchy sesame-soy dressing.
steps: Cook the soba noodles in boiling water for 5 minutes, adding the broccoli for the final 2 minutes.
Add the edamame for the final 1 minute. Drain and rinse everything with cold water.
Whisk together the sesame oil, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and crushed garlic.
Halve the cucumber lengthways and slice thinly.
Toss the noodles, broccoli, edamame, and cucumber together with the dressing.
Serve topped with spring onions and sesame seeds.
tips: This dish is equally good warm or cold — ideal for packed lunches.
Add a tbsp of peanut butter to the dressing for a richer sauce.
A fresh red chilli adds great heat.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days — dressing may need re-stirring.
reheating: Serve cold or at room temperature.

title: Quick Egg Fried Rice
description: Speedy, satisfying egg fried rice — better than a takeaway and ready in 15 minutes.
steps: Dice the carrot finely. Heat the wok over very high heat with vegetable oil.
Fry the carrot for 2 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger, stir for 30 seconds.
Push everything to one side. Crack in the eggs and scramble.
Add the cold rice and break up any clumps. Toss to combine.
Add the frozen peas and soy sauce. Stir-fry for 2 more minutes.
Drizzle with sesame oil. Serve topped with sliced spring onions.
tips: Day-old cold rice is the secret — freshly cooked rice will be too wet and clump.
Microwave rice pouches work perfectly here.
Gochujang or sriracha drizzled on top is excellent.
storage: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.
reheating: Reheat in a hot wok with a splash of water.

title: Spicy Black Bean Rice Bowl
description: Fluffy rice topped with smoky black beans, creamy avocado, and fresh coriander.
steps: Cook the basmati rice.
Drain and rinse the black beans. Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Cook the minced garlic for 1 minute. Add the black beans, cumin, and smoked paprika.
Cook for 5 minutes, roughly mashing some of the beans. Season well and add a squeeze of lime.
Finely dice the red onion and slice the avocado.
Divide rice between bowls, top with the black beans, avocado, and diced red onion.
Finish with fresh coriander, lime juice, and extra chilli if desired.
tips: Mashing some beans makes the mixture nicely saucy.
Add pickled jalapeños for instant heat.
A spoonful of sour cream or yoghurt makes this even better.
storage: Rice and beans keep for 3 days. Slice avocado fresh.
reheating: Reheat beans and rice separately.

title: Halloumi & Roasted Veg Couscous
description: Golden halloumi with fluffy lemon couscous and roasted Mediterranean vegetables.
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C. Chop the peppers, courgette, and red onion into chunks.
Toss veg and cherry tomatoes in 2 tbsp olive oil and season. Roast for 20 minutes.
Put couscous in a bowl. Pour over hot stock, cover, and leave for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Add lemon zest, lemon juice, and 1 tbsp olive oil to the couscous. Season and mix.
Slice the halloumi and fry in a dry pan over high heat for 2 minutes each side until golden.
Serve couscous topped with roasted veg, halloumi, and torn fresh mint.
tips: No need to oil the halloumi — it has enough fat to fry in a dry pan.
Couscous absorbs flavours brilliantly — add dried fruits or pine nuts for variety.
Leftover couscous makes an excellent packed lunch the next day.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge. Slice halloumi fresh.
reheating: Couscous is good cold. Reheat roasted veg in the oven for 5 minutes.

title: Smoky Black Bean Tacos
description: Crispy corn tortillas filled with smoky chipotle beans, fresh avocado, and lime.
steps: Drain and rinse the black beans. Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Add the beans, chipotle paste, and smoked paprika. Cook for 5 minutes, mashing some beans.
Season with salt and a squeeze of lime. Keep warm.
Warm tortillas in a dry frying pan for 30 seconds each side.
Mash the avocado with lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Finely slice the red onion.
Assemble tacos with beans, avocado, red onion, coriander, and a dollop of sour cream.
tips: Char the tortillas directly over a gas flame for an authentic smoky flavour.
Quick-pickled red onion (in lime juice for 10 minutes) is a game changer.
Shredded cabbage adds great crunch.
storage: Bean filling keeps for 3 days. Assemble tacos fresh.
reheating: Reheat bean mixture in a pan. Warm tortillas in a dry pan.

title: Halloumi & Roasted Pepper Wraps
description: Golden halloumi with sweet roasted peppers and creamy hummus in a warm flatbread.
steps: Slice the halloumi 1cm thick. Fry in a dry pan over high heat for 2 minutes each side until golden.
Finely slice the red onion. Warm the flatbreads in the same pan for 30 seconds.
Spread hummus generously over each flatbread.
Layer with baby spinach, roasted peppers, and red onion.
Top with the fried halloumi and squeeze over some lemon juice.
Roll up and serve immediately.
tips: Drizzle with chilli sauce or harissa for extra heat.
Add sliced cucumber for freshness.
Jarred roasted peppers are a great weeknight shortcut — always worth keeping in the cupboard.
storage: Wrap filling keeps for 2 days. Assemble fresh.
reheating: Re-fry halloumi slices briefly if making ahead.

title: Cheesy Bean Quesadillas
description: Crispy golden tortillas packed with melted cheddar and smoky black beans.
steps: Drain and roughly mash the black beans. Dice the pepper and red onion finely.
Mix beans, diced veg, paprika, and half the cheese together.
Spread the mixture over 2 tortillas. Top each with remaining cheese and a second tortilla.
Heat a little oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Cook each quesadilla for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and crispy.
Slice into wedges and serve with sour cream and a green salad.
tips: Press the quesadilla down with a spatula while cooking for even browning.
Add pickled jalapeños or fresh chilli for heat.
Guacamole or salsa makes a brilliant accompaniment.
storage: Best eaten fresh.
reheating: Reheat in a dry pan for 1-2 minutes each side to re-crisp.

title: Roasted Tomato & Garlic Soup
description: Deeply flavoured roasted tomato soup with golden garlic — infinitely better than tinned.
steps: Dice the onion and slice the garlic. Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Soften the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and stock. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Blend until completely smooth. Season generously.
Stir in the cream and most of the basil.
Toast the sourdough. Serve soup with toast, a drizzle of olive oil, and remaining basil.
tips: A pinch of sugar balances the acidity beautifully.
For extra depth, add a tablespoon of balsamic vinegar.
This soup freezes brilliantly — make a double batch.
storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge. Freezes for 3 months.
reheating: Reheat in a pan, stirring occasionally.

title: Spiced Butternut Squash Soup
description: Silky, warming butternut squash soup with coconut milk and warming spices.
steps: Peel the butternut squash and dice into 3cm chunks. Dice the onion.
Heat olive oil in a large pan. Cook onion for 5 minutes. Add garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add cumin and coriander, stir for 30 seconds. Add the squash.
Pour in the stock, bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes until squash is tender.
Add the coconut milk, then blend until smooth. Season well.
Serve with warm crusty bread rolls.
tips: Buy pre-prepared diced squash to save time.
A swirl of cream or yoghurt makes a beautiful garnish.
Toasted pumpkin seeds on top add excellent crunch.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days. Freezes well.
reheating: Reheat in a pan, adding extra stock if needed.

title: Tuscan White Bean & Spinach Soup
description: Rustic, hearty Italian soup with cannellini beans, spinach, and rosemary.
steps: Dice the onion and finely slice the garlic. Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add garlic and rosemary, stir for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomatoes and stock. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Drain and rinse the cannellini beans. Add half the beans whole and mash the other half.
Add all beans to the pan and simmer for 10 minutes. Stir in the spinach to wilt.
Season well. Serve with toasted sourdough and parmesan.
tips: Mashing half the beans creates a naturally thick, creamy broth.
A drizzle of good olive oil on top is traditional and delicious.
Add a parmesan rind to the simmering soup for incredible depth.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
reheating: Reheat in a pan with extra stock.

title: Spiced Red Lentil Soup
description: A warming, spiced red lentil soup with smoky paprika and a squeeze of fresh lemon.
steps: Dice the onion and carrot. Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Cook onion and carrot for 5 minutes. Add garlic and all spices, stir for 1 minute.
Rinse the lentils and add to the pan with the stock.
Bring to a boil then simmer for 20 minutes until lentils have dissolved.
Season well and add a generous squeeze of lemon juice.
Serve with warm crusty bread.
tips: This soup thickens as it sits — add extra stock when reheating.
A drizzle of chilli oil on top is wonderful.
Blend smooth or keep chunky — both are delicious.
storage: Keeps for 4 days in the fridge. Freezes beautifully.
reheating: Reheat in a pan with extra stock.

title: Mediterranean Veg Tray Bake
description: Colourful roasted Mediterranean vegetables with golden halloumi and crumbled feta.
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C. Chop all veg into similar-sized chunks.
Toss veg in olive oil, oregano, salt, and pepper on a large baking tray.
Roast for 20 minutes.
Slice the halloumi and nestle into the veg. Roast for another 15 minutes until golden.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and crumble over the feta.
Serve with flatbreads or crusty bread.
tips: Don't overcrowd the tray — use two trays if needed for better browning.
A drizzle of balsamic vinegar at the end adds great depth.
Leftovers are brilliant in a wrap or pita the next day.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
reheating: Reheat in a 180°C oven for 10 minutes.

title: Crispy Chickpea & Sweet Potato Tray
description: Oven-crisped chickpeas with caramelised sweet potato, topped with a tahini drizzle.
steps: Preheat oven to 210°C. Drain chickpeas and dry very well with kitchen paper.
Cube sweet potato and slice red onion.
Toss chickpeas, sweet potato, and onion in olive oil, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Spread on a large baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, shaking halfway, until chickpeas are crispy.
Whisk tahini with lemon juice and 2 tbsp water until smooth.
Serve over a bed of baby spinach, drizzled with tahini dressing.
tips: The drier the chickpeas, the crispier they get — don't skip this step.
Add a handful of cherry tomatoes for the last 10 minutes.
Serve with flatbread or pitta to make this more filling.
storage: Keeps for 2 days. Chickpeas lose their crispness in the fridge.
reheating: Reheat in a 200°C oven for 8 minutes to re-crisp.

title: Pesto Gnocchi Tray Bake
description: Pillowy gnocchi roasted with cherry tomatoes, courgette, and melted mozzarella.
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve the cherry tomatoes and slice courgette and pepper.
Put the gnocchi, tomatoes, courgette, and pepper into a large baking tray.
Drizzle with olive oil and season well. Toss to coat.
Roast for 15 minutes. Remove and add dollops of pesto throughout.
Tear over the mozzarella and return to the oven for 10 more minutes until golden.
Scatter with fresh basil and serve straight from the tray.
tips: No boiling needed — the gnocchi roasts beautifully straight from the packet.
Use shop-bought pesto — it's absolutely fine for this.
Pine nuts scattered over before the final roast add lovely crunch.
storage: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge.
reheating: Reheat in oven at 180°C for 10 minutes.

title: Easy Veggie Chilli
description: A hearty, smoky chilli loaded with beans, peppers, and warming spices — brilliant for batch cooking.
steps: Cook the rice. Dice the onion and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan. Cook onion and pepper for 5 minutes.
Add garlic and all spices. Stir for 1 minute.
Add both beans (drained), chopped tomatoes, and stock.
Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick.
Season well. Serve over rice with sour cream and grated cheddar.
tips: A square of dark chocolate stirred in at the end adds incredible depth.
Leftovers are even better the next day.
Use as a filling for baked potatoes or serve with cornbread.
storage: Keeps in the fridge for 4 days. Freezes for 3 months.
reheating: Reheat in a pan with a splash of water.

title: Classic Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a rich, spiced tomato and pepper sauce — easy and deeply satisfying.
equipment: Large lidded frying pan or skillet
steps: Dice the onion and slice the pepper. Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat.
Cook onion and pepper for 7 minutes until soft. Add garlic, cumin, paprika, and harissa.
Stir for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes. Season and simmer for 5 minutes.
Make 4 wells in the sauce. Crack an egg into each well.
Cover and cook on a gentle simmer for 5-7 minutes until whites are just set.
Crumble over feta and serve straight from the pan with crusty bread.
tips: Keep a lid on — the steam cooks the eggs from above.
Remove from heat while yolks are still runny — they continue cooking in the pan.
Fresh coriander or parsley scattered over before serving is lovely.
storage: Best eaten fresh. The sauce keeps for 3 days.
reheating: Reheat the sauce and poach fresh eggs in it.

title: Tomato & Halloumi Flatbread Pizzas
description: Quick and cheesy flatbread pizzas with golden halloumi — ready in 15 minutes.
steps: Preheat grill to high (or oven to 220°C).
Mix the chopped tomatoes with crushed garlic, dried oregano, and a pinch of salt.
Spread the tomato sauce over each flatbread.
Slice the halloumi thinly and arrange over the sauce. Add halved cherry tomatoes.
Drizzle with olive oil. Grill for 5-7 minutes until halloumi is golden and edges crispy.
Top with fresh basil and serve immediately.
tips: Swap halloumi for mozzarella for a more classic pizza feel.
Add rocket on top just before serving for a peppery kick.
Use naan breads instead of flatbreads for a thicker base.
storage: Best eaten immediately.
reheating: Reheat in a hot oven for 5 minutes.

title: Smoky Mac & Cheese
description: Deeply cheesy macaroni with smoked paprika and a crunchy golden breadcrumb topping.
steps: Cook the macaroni in salted water until al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water before draining.
In the same pan, melt butter over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk until smooth. Simmer for 3 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Remove from heat. Add grated cheddar, paprika, and mustard powder. Stir until melted.
Add the pasta back in with a splash of pasta water. Stir well. Season.
Top with breadcrumbs and sliced spring onions. Grill for 3 minutes for a golden top (optional).
tips: Grating your own cheddar melts far better than pre-grated.
Add a splash of hot sauce or Worcestershire sauce to the cheese sauce.
For added veg, stir in frozen peas with the pasta.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
reheating: Reheat in a pan with a splash of milk to loosen.

title: Korean-Style Veggie Bibimbap
description: A colourful bowl of seasoned rice and vegetables with a fried egg and gochujang.
steps: Cook the rice according to packet instructions.
Julienne (or grate) the carrot and courgette. Slice mushrooms.
In a pan with a little sesame oil, sauté each vegetable separately with a little garlic and soy sauce. Set each aside.
Wilt the spinach with sesame oil and a pinch of salt.
Fry the eggs sunny-side-up.
Divide rice between bowls. Arrange veg in sections around the bowl.
Top each with a fried egg. Drizzle with gochujang mixed with a little sesame oil.
tips: Prepping each veg separately is key to the authentic bibimbap experience.
Mix everything together vigorously at the table — that's part of the ritual.
Adjust gochujang to taste — it can be very spicy.
storage: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Fry fresh eggs when serving.
reheating: Reheat rice and veg separately, top with fresh egg.

title: Falafel & Hummus Wraps
description: Crispy shop-bought falafel with creamy hummus, fresh salad, and lemon in warm flatbreads.
steps: Heat falafel according to packet instructions — either bake in the oven or fry.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan for 30 seconds each side.
Slice the cucumber, tomato, and red onion.
Spread hummus generously over each flatbread.
Layer with spinach, cucumber, tomato, and red onion.
Add the warm falafel, squeeze over lemon juice, and roll up to serve.
tips: Making your own falafel is great but shop-bought works perfectly for weeknights.
Harissa or hot sauce adds a welcome kick.
Add pickled red cabbage for extra crunch and acidity.
storage: Assemble fresh. Falafel keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
reheating: Reheat falafel in a hot oven for 8 minutes.

title: Halloumi & Aubergine Tray Bake
description: Sticky roasted aubergine and halloumi with cherry tomatoes and balsamic glaze.
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cube aubergine, slice red onion, and chop pepper.
Toss aubergine, onion, and pepper in olive oil, oregano, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast for 15 minutes. Add the cherry tomatoes and drizzle with balsamic.
Slice the halloumi thickly and nestle into the veg. Roast for 15 more minutes until golden.
Warm the flatbreads in the oven for the final 3 minutes.
Serve the traybake over warm flatbreads.
tips: Salt the aubergine for 10 minutes before roasting to draw out moisture, if you have time.
A drizzle of tahini or yoghurt sauce over the top is excellent.
Add a handful of fresh herbs at the end — parsley or mint work beautifully.
storage: Keeps for 3 days in the fridge.
reheating: Reheat in oven at 180°C for 10 minutes.

title: Singapore-Style Noodles
description: Fragrant, lightly curried rice vermicelli with egg, peppers, and spring onions.
steps: Soak the rice vermicelli in boiling water for 3 minutes, then drain.
Julienne the carrot and slice the pepper and spring onions.
Heat a wok over very high heat with oil. Stir-fry carrot and pepper for 2 minutes.
Push to one side and scramble the eggs. Add garlic and chilli, stir for 30 seconds.
Add the drained noodles and curry powder. Toss everything together.
Add soy sauce and spring onions. Toss for 1 more minute and serve.
tips: Use mild curry powder unless you enjoy heat.
Frozen veg (peas, sweetcorn) can be added straight from the bag.
Bean sprouts added at the very end add great texture.
storage: Best eaten fresh.
reheating: Reheat in a hot wok with a splash of water.
